title: Onboarding checklist → 90-day churn
teaser: CSMs chose accounts; progress on the checklist is a result, not a cause.
question: Did the new onboarding checklist reduce churn in the first 90 days?
ask: We need churned accounts per 100 to size the rollout.

treatment.name: got_checklist
treatment.meaning: 1 = account was given the onboarding checklist

variables.name: week1_active_users
variables.meaning: users active in the first week
variables.recorded: end of week 1, before the checklist decision

hidden.name: U_health
hidden.label: how committed the customer's team is

hidden.name: U_atrisk
hidden.label: CSMs' private read of which customers were about to leave

notes.text: Customer success managers decided which accounts got the checklist, usually bigger or more active ones.
Only accounts that got the checklist can complete items.
CSMs mostly gave the checklist to accounts they felt were at risk of leaving, based on calls and emails we don't log.

traps.name: Consequence column
traps.text: checklist_items_done exists only for checklist accounts and tracks engagement.

traps.name: Selection on early activity
traps.text: CSMs picked more active accounts; week-1 activity must be adjusted for.

traps.name: Collider
traps.text: NPS at day 60 is shaped by both the checklist and churn risk.

traps.name: Unrecorded at-risk judgement
traps.text: CSMs targeted accounts they privately judged at risk; nothing recorded captures it.
